blocks.content: Course: React Hooks: Level Up Your First Web App
Now, we'll import useFetch() and call it. Here's what will happen:

items: The raw API response comes back as data.
A useMemo() then maps it into the entries shape the rest of the app expects.
The useMemo() will have a guard so that data starts as null on the first render, before the fetch completes. Without it, calling .map() on null would throw an error.

Here's the changes you'll see in the code:

items: useEffect(), refreshKey, and handleRefresh() are gone.
The Refresh button is also temporarily removed. The practice at the end of this lesson will add a refetch() function to useFetch() and restore it.

blocks.content: Click Run Code. The app behaves exactly as before. The fetch logic is now in one place.
